edges.notes: DWARF debug data is typically stored in ELF sections (.debug_*).
LLVM backends emit ELF relocatable objects and linked images on common Unix targets.
Linux exec path loads ELF binaries and interprets ELF program headers.
UKI construction wraps a Linux kernel that remains ELF-shaped inside the PE UKI envelope.
C/C++ toolchains on Unix-class systems predominantly emit ELF objects.
RISC-V ELF psABI and ELF flags are specified alongside the ISA (platform docs).
Debug adapters resolve symbols via debug info commonly packaged in ELF objects.
readelf, objdump, ld, and as are the common operational interface to ELF objects in GNU/Linux flows.
lld consumes and emits ELF on typical Unix-class LLVM toolchains.
Clang emits ELF relocatable objects on typical Unix-class targets.
GCC emits ELF relocatable objects and executables on typical Unix-class GNU flows.
GDB loads ELF executables and shared libraries for debugging.
LLDB loads ELF binaries and shared libraries on Linux.
libc.so and the dynamic linker are ELF shared objects; PT_INTERP links loader to executables on GNU/Linux.
musl libc.so and ld-musl are ELF shared objects on musl-based Linux systems.
libstdc++.so is an ELF shared library on typical GNU/Linux targets.
libc++.so (and related) are ELF shared libraries on typical LLVM libc++ Unix targets.
libc++abi.so is an ELF shared library on typical LLVM C++ ABI Unix targets.
Alpine Linux userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
Debian userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
Ubuntu userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
Fedora userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
RHEL userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
Rocky Linux userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
AlmaLinux userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
CentOS Stream userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
Historical CentOS Linux userland binaries and shared libraries were ELF on typical Linux targets.
FreeBSD libc and typical FreeBSD userland binaries use ELF dynamic linking on supported architectures.
OpenBSD libc and typical OpenBSD userland binaries use ELF dynamic linking on supported architectures.
NetBSD libc and typical NetBSD userland binaries use ELF dynamic linking on supported architectures.
DragonFly libc and typical DragonFly userland binaries use ELF dynamic linking on supported architectures.
illumos libc and typical illumos userland binaries use ELF dynamic linking on supported architectures.
Bionic and typical Android native binaries use ELF dynamic linking on supported ABIs.
Embedded link flows commonly emit ELF relocatable objects and images linking newlib archives on ELF-capable targets.
